newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 11.

text.p: Morgan finally says sorry, future on hold till SFO report: NZ First MP leader Winston Peters shrank from a possible showdown with his assertive Maori MPs on Tuesday and gave Tukoroirangi Morgan yet another chance. Page 1.
Committee criticises Housing NZ: Housing NZ has been criticised for failing to maintain some of its properties, by Parliament's social services committee. Page 2.

Funding agency 'should have aired concerns': Maori broadcasting funding agency Te Mangai Paho should have taken its concerns about Aotearoa Television Network's finances to its minister immediately, Parliament's commerce select committee said on Tuesday. Page 2.
Aussie firm reaps $1m in Conservation rejig: An Australian consultancy firm will reap more than $1 million for its work on the restructuring of the Conservation Department. Page 2.

Optimism softened and smudged, says Birch: The perception that the government was dominated by scandal and ignoring spending restraints was a drag on New Zealand's economic and social performance, Finance Minister Bill Birch said on Tuesday. Page 12.

Telecom tipped to shed another 400: Further restructuring within Telecom could see as many as 400 people lose their jobs during the next three years, according to Singapore-based analysts with brokerage Morgan Stanley. Page 13.

Gold Coast sharks rip off Kiwis, Queensland property no golden nest egg: Gullible New Zealanders are proving easy fodder for Gold Coast land sharks who are ripping investors off by up to $60,000 a deal.
Skellerup bonds find keen buyer: Melbourne firm offers $702 each: Skellerup bond holders are being invited to sell their holdings by a Melbourne-based investor specialising in troubled companies.

Takeover threat to power servicers: Contractors and service providers to Auckland electricity companies are expected to be the losers when details of a takeover offer for Power New Zealand are issued.

Fernz applies more pressure: Fernz Corp has stepped up discussions with French chemical giant Rhone Poulenc to see how the two companies might split up the $1 billion worldwide market for the agricultural chemical bromoxynil.
Freedom looking to expand mortgage base: National Mutual subsidiary Freedom Financial Services intends expanding as mortgage book by relaunching the telephone based direct distribution company.
Record profit by GreenFields: Timaru-based GreenFields Co-operative has announced a record profit of $525,857 for the year to March 31, up 1.4 percent on the previous year. Page 27.
Manpower in Chch: Manpower, the world's biggest employment company, has opened an office in Christchurch. Page 28.
